# Forest of Hate

*Pages PDF 3-32*

## **Introduction**
A disease called Eyeslime Fever has infected settlements in the eastern Laurelorn forest. Shallyans have failed to contain the plague, and herbal remedies are scarce. If the Characters cannot discover a way to prevent an epidemic, war and chaos will devastate the Laurelorn causing Nordland’s logging industry to collapse and even deadlier plagues to spread. The Characters are medicine-seekers who find themselves facing not just disease, but also propaganda, prejudice, and profane sorcery. 

**Forest of Hate** is intended for a party of 4-6 experienced characters in the second or third tier of a Career. Wood Elf characters may face difficulties among humans, but parties that do not include a Eonir character will find the scenario more challenging. 

Even if profiteering is the party’s initial motive, many may find themselves hard-pressed to stand by and tolerate the injustices they witness. However, even good intentions can sometimes serve the Ruinous Powers… 

Although Forest of Hate makes an excellent standalone adventure, it works well as a precursor to Laurelorn Forest campaigns using the information in **Archives of the Empire: Vol. 1** . The scenario begins on the road leading north from Middenheim. GMs wishing to insert this scenario into **The Enemy Within** campaign can choose a friendly NPC from **Power Behind the Throne** to be an early victim of the Fever, pointing the way to this adventure. With minor adjustments to the beginning of **The Horned Rat** , this adventure would work well just after the events of **Power** . **Behind the Throne** 

## **Ancient Background**
A swathe of blighted vine grew around the crystal sarcophagus as Chaos magic seeped slowly from the ward into the forest around the villa’s gardens. Meanwhile, the Elves were preoccupied with rebuilding Tor Lithanel, so the incidents at Ammenvale were forgotten by most. 

The present crisis traces its roots to the Laurelorn’s ancient history and forgotten Elven arcana. Most Elves would postulate that Eonir — Wood Elf — culture emerged from the War of the Beard 2,600 years ago. In truth, exiled Elven mages had led some colonists down a path divergent from their siblings in Ulthaun centuries prior. The very first outbreak of what would become Eyeslime Fever was introduced by one of these mysterious figures who was willing to sacrifice his ideals, even his soul, for victory over the hated Dwarfs. 

## **Eonir Coverup**
Centuries later, devotees of the god Asuryan rediscovered Ammenvale and made inquiries after it, learning of Darlorhan from his only surviving apprentice. She had indeed avoided the taint of corruption, but in her innocence the former apprentice, now a respected leader of Eonir, recalled Darlorhan only as a wise and powerful wizard who knew the forest sprits well and worked for the betterment of his kin. They designated the site a holy sanctuary, recognised Darlorhan as respected elder, and vowed to protect the wizard in his crystal tomb. The Daemons that occasionally lurked in the surrounding woods, like most ills, were attributed to human encroachments. 

## **War of the Beard**
Near the end of the War of the Beard, Dwarf armies had destroyed Kor Immarmor and threatened to overrun the last remaining Elf colony at Tor Lithanel. In the Elves’ hour of desperation, the exiled mages summoned a great spirit-host to rout the besiegers. Meanwhile, a solitary wizard named Darlorhan unleashed a terrible disease at the ruins of Kor Immarmor where Dwarf reserves were encamped. 

Chaos taint crept so gradually from Ammenvale that for centuries Darlorhan’s dark past remained buried. However, there were some Eonir elders who’d lived during the War of the Beard and still remembered what happened at Kor Immarmor. They wondered of the spirit who had helped Darlorhan to develop his plague and why it had never been seen again. As Daemons haunted the forest in ever greater numbers, the cult of Asuryan ensured that no trespasser would find the sanctuary at Ammenvale and disturb the experiments concealed within. 

The two-pronged Elven assault broke the Dwarfs’ resolve and ultimately forced them to withdraw to their mountain holds. Though the war continued for years afterwards, the Dwarfs never again threatened Tor Lithanel. Kor Immarmor was recorded in the Book of Grudges as the site of an atrocity committed by an Elf dubbed the ‘The Blinding Death’. 

## **Nurgle’s Corruption**
## **Present Situation**
After the Dwarf retreat, one of the nature spirits that had aided Darlorhan in creating the disease that drove off the Dwarfs revealed itself to be a Daemon of Nurgle. Horrified at what he had done, but knowing his soul was already damned, Darlorhan acted quickly. He destroyed all of his research, gathered up his deadly experiments, and — with an equal measure of regret and cold efficiency — slew all of his apprentices save the most junior, whom he hoped had not yet been subject to Nurgle’s corruption. 

Two millennia later, Elves still guard the Laurelorn’s secrets from Nordlanders, with whom they now share the forest. Ammenvale is just one of many sites upon which human trespassers are forbidden. Few Elves have seen Ammenvale firsthand, but those who know of its existence trust the cult of Asuryan to keep vigil. Even as Red Blight — a fungal disease that infects trees — spreads from the tainted wood nearby, Ammenvale’s guardians insist the magical ward surrounding the villa has not been compromised. In a way, they are right — the comprimised ward keeps the touch of Chaos out of Ammenvale, but does so by amplifying and spreading its foul presence in the vicinity. 

Then, Darlorhan encased himself in crystal at Ammenvale as a final act of penance to empower a magical ward — the ancient Shield of Asuryan — that would seal away his terrible creations. He hoped it might also preserve him from further corruption, though in this, as in much else, he was mistaken. 

by amplifying and spreading its foul presence in the vicinity.

Darlorhan’s precautions at Ammenvale could not prevent Nurgle from claiming the wizard. He became a vessel of corruption, and over the long centuries the Shield of Asuryan was turned from a ward against Chaos into a conduit for it. 

## **New Outbreaks**
Red Blight was first reported a year ago, growing on trees in rural Nordland. Foresters called it the ‘fey curse’ because Spites — minor forest spirits — are sometimes sighted near their logging camps at night. Several months later, cases of Eyeslime Fever began spreading through villages in the eastern Laurelorn. As the disease seemed to infect loggers who had contact with trees infected by the Red Blight, the two infections have become associated. Many locals blame the Elves, whom they claim spread the disease to prevent logging. 

In truth, the ward at Ammenvale has allowed the influence of Nurgle to spread. As the Plaugefather’s presence grows, his servants flock to spread his gifts far and wide. Darlorhan’s naïve protectors, the cult of Asuryan, have prevented anyone from seriously investigating Ammenvale or its surroundings, and a tiny fragment of Nurgle’s garden has begun to manifest nearby. Daemons, masquerading as tree spirits, have overtaken the tainted wood, revived Eyeslime fever out of a twisted respect for Darlorhan, and begun to spread it with the help of Nurgle’s human cultists. 

## **Profiteers and Liars**
Nordland’s logging villages are plague-ridden and its sawmills are closed. Idle foresters are joining a popular new guild that blames the Elves for the spread of Eyeslime Fever, among other bizarre theories. The Wood Elves widely refute the guild’s rhetoric, contending that human logging encroachments have caused the Red Blight, and Laurelorn is on the verge of war. 

In recent weeks, plague medicine has become a lucrative commodity. Enterprising herbalists and physicians are favouring wealthy towns but leaving rural folk to fend for themselves. Charlatans tour the region peddling fake cures, and bounty hunters scour the forest for locks of Elf hair to sell as charms. 

## **Quest for a Cure**
Nurgle’s corruption creates a noxious tangle of moral dilemmas and unintended consequences which the players must navigate if they wish to resolve the situation in Nordland. Those who have already tried have been killed, lost, or lured into making a profit from the fear and confusion. While blame is placed on Elf and Human alike, the true sources of Eyeslime Fever remain hidden, protected by the cult of Asuryan. Players may sensibly focus on finding a true cure for the disease and distributing it, but this alone cannot prevent a war. The sources of Nurgle’s corruption must also be destroyed and his champions defeated. However, each battle the Characters win might play into another Nurglish scheme. Success hinges upon discovering which factions serve the Plague Lord without falling victim to him. 

## Grubile and the Realms of Chaos
Grubile the Inhabited is a Great Unclean One, one of Nurgle’s most beloved servants. While it is not uncommon for the body of one of Nurgle’s servants to play host to a variety of terrible parasites and spores, Grubile the Inhabited is notably riven with such creatures. Nurglings dance and cavort about his flesh, carving fresh, bile-spewing tunnels through bilious tissue to converse with their chittering neighbours. Grubile the Inhabited is notoriously proud and protective of his many ‘children’, and is repaid by their fervent search within him for ever more exotic and spectacular plagues and diseases. 

When a Nurgling finds an interesting disease, it carefully infects itself and carries the blessed plague to Grubile for consideration. If the Great Unclean One approves, the creature’s fellows exult in celebration, and Grubile’s leathery skin undulates hideously with their joyous dancing. Sometimes these are novel infections, but more often they are an old and half forgotten malady Grubile aquired centuries ago. 

So it is with Eyeslime Fever, which Grubile is reviving from dormancy, intent on improving its lethality against the Dwarfs — whom are by nature quite resistant to Nurgle’s many gifts. His loyal herald, the Daemon Mulch-Rot, has prepared the testing ground and enlisted human agents. In the Garden of Blight, Grubile keeps the soul of an Elf entangled in vines. Grubile used trickery to ensnare the desperate Darlorhan, a powerful mage, during the War of the Beard. 

Despite the long centuries, the Elf still retains some connection to his former home in the Laurelorn forest. While this has preserved some element of his sanity, it has also allowed Grubile to influence the mortal realm. His most useful mortal servants have been unwitting members of the cult of Asuryan, who mistakingly believe the whispers they hear from Darlorhan’s crystal tomb come from the sleeping wizard himself. 

## **Running the Adventure**
**Forest of Hate** is a sandbox adventure, with details given on the various factions and their goals, as well as the situation in various settlements throughout the area. There is no single path through these events, and you are encouraged to be flexible in how your players tackle the adventure. Nevertheless, there are a number of events which are likely to occur, though possibly not in the order given below. 

## **Learning About the Situation**
The Characters learn about the disease, its effect on the region, and perhaps the political situation between Nordland’s loggers and the Wood Elves, if they were not already aware. How this is handled is up to the GM. If the adventure is being run as a one off, you may simply start with your party on the road to Nordland. If it is part of an ongoing campaign, then tales of ill-fortune in the northern province are sure to be spoken of in inns and taverns around the Empire. 

## **Further Research**
Once they begin looking into things, Characters should quickly become aware of some of the major factions at play, especially the Jolly Axemen and their leader, Herr Kochler, and their attitude toward the disease. Other influential groups and individuals are discussed in **Important Individuals and Groups,** below. Characters may also become aware of the various cures that have been proposed for the disease, and begin gathering and trading some of them, as there is a good deal of money to be made. See **Adventure Locations** on page 21 for a more detailed guide to the region’s settlements. 

## **Crossing the Demst**
At some point, the Characters will become aware that the answer to the disease lies somewhere in the Laurelorn, and they will have to cross the river Demst to explore there. The forest is dangerous and full of perils — see **Encounters** on page 22 for more. 

## **Assault on Ammenvale**
An ancient Old One site, protected by an an arcane Elven ward, Ammenvale is the centre of the outbreak, and the fissure by which the influence of Nurgle is seeping into the world. At its heart the body of Darlorhan still lies, suffused with the power of Nurgle still whispering commands to his servants, both witting and unwitting. Darlorhan must be destroyed, and difficult decisions made. 

## **Dealing with the Fallout**
Depending on their actions, the Characters may face several difficult decisions. While the ward at Ammenvale is the source of the corruption, it also serves to contain horrors of its own. If it is destroyed the the site will become subject to the Winds of Magic, useless as a site for research, and more importantly, freeing the diseases held within. The Characters may have to decide how to handle this, and the effects on Nordland will have dire consequences for decades to come. On top of this, Nurgle’s mortal servants and lackies must be dealt with, lest they continue to spread corruption throughout the land. This may be more difficult than it first appears, however, as they are well connected and terribly charismatic. 

Finally, even if the Characters stop the plague, Nordland may still end up at war with the Elves of the Laurelorn unless things are handled discreetly, and the right people on both sides find out the truth of the matter. 

## **Figures of Note**
This scenario features two cults based in the Laurelorn Forest. The Sons of Asuryan are just one of the several cults of Asuryan in Elf society. Fanatical warriors, these once proud devotees of Asuryan have been led astray by what they believe to be the spirit of Darlorhan, whom they refer to as The Hermit Lord. 

The Nordland Foresters’ Guild is a cult of profiteers and agitators pretending to act in the interests of woodsmen. Although the two cults are enemies, they ultimately serve the same master in Grubile the Inhabited, a greater daemon of Nurgle. 

## **The Cult of Asuryan**
The creator god Asuryan is the ruler of the Elven pantheon and governs balance in all things. In the Laurelorn Forest, disciples of Asuryan are dedicated to preserving their god’s plan. Eonir prophets rarely claim to understand the intentions of a god, but nevertheless they believe the arcane wonders left behind by the Old Ones are integral to his plan.  Here they named themselves ‘The Sons of Asuryan’, and made it their mandate to rediscover and secure any lost Old One sites. 

## **The Sons of Asuryan**
Ammenvale was the first site reclaimed by the Sons. Scouts had reported that a great protective ward — which they dubbed the Shield of Asuryan — was still operational, protecting whatever may have lain within the structure. The nearby ruins of Kor Immarmor were recolonized, and a small party of Sons appointed to garrison Ammenvale. 

In recent centuries, Ulthuan’s Loremasters have taken over stewardship of leylines within the Empire, and the cult of Asuryan has greatly declined in influence in the Laurelorn. Only the garrison at Ammenvale still bear the name The Sons of Asuryan, but their commitment to their ancient duty has not faltered. Without guidance from the seers of Lileath, the Sons of Asuryan have increasingly turned to the voice of the Hermit Lord for instruction. Over time, the group has become increasingly insular and convinced of its own righteousness. Its members remain unaware that Darlorhan is a puppet of Nurgle. 

Sons of Asuryan rarely speak, favouring hand signals to communicate with one another — they believe silence allows them to better hear the words of their master. Verbal negotiation with trespassers is handled by the patrol leader. They are dangerous, and ultimately tools of Nurgle, but they do not know this. If it were revealed, the Sons would surely disband, or be ripped asunder in shame and infighting. 

## **Darlorhan**
**The Hermit Lord, The Blinding Death, Puppet of Nurgle** 

The Elven archmage Darlorhan is over 4,000 years old, though only if one considers his current state of being to constitute life. In the age before the War of the Beard, he lived as a hermit experimenting with Laurelorn’s exotic flora. Although Darlorhan’s reclusiveness earned him the epithet ‘The Hermit Lord’, he was one of the few wizards capable of binding departed Elven souls into trees to preserve them from Chaos. Darlorhan chose the site of Ammenvale for his work because it was shielded by an ancient ward that turned aside the influence of Chaos completely. 

During the later years of the War of the Beard, Darlorhan unexpectedly unleashed a deadly disease on the Dwarf invaders. In the Eonir’s hour of desperation, the mage had unknowingly struck a bargain with dark powers to complete his research. Today, Darlorhan’s body is preserved in crystal at Ammenvale, where the Shield of Asuryan is sustained by his magical essence. Though his body cannot move or speak, it is believed that the ‘Hermit Lord’ can still issue instructions to devoted guardians, the Sons of Asuryan, by magical means. However, the voice adherents hear is actually Grubile, a daemon of Nurgle. 

## **Nordland Foresters’ Guild**
Until this year, the Nordland timber trade wasn’t represented by a guild. However, after the first instances of Red Blight were reported, a wealthy merchant named Oswald Kochler established the Nordland Foresters’ Guild to advocate for local woodsmen. Kochler is currently touring the logging villages to recruit members. The guild office in Salzenmund is staffed by a lone scribe, while Guildmaster Kochler campaigns from his illegal logging camp in Vesterrup. Unwitting bargains with ruinous powers have granted certain members immunity to Eyeslime Fever — or at least to its effects. As the plague ravages entire villages, Kochler and his rural agitators spread misinformation. According to their version of the truth, Eyeslime Fever is a conspiracy by Wood Elves to drive loggers away from the Laurelorn forest. 

## **Herr Oswald Kochler**
## **Forester Guildmaster**
Herr Kochler is a prominent timber merchant and Salzenmund city councillor, who owns logging camps near the Laurelorn village of Vesterrup. He recently founded the Nordland Foresters’ Guild to represent woodsmen and protest logging quotas imposed by Elves. Kochler has always been ruthless, and is not above working with the likes of Goblins and other enemies of the Empire if it aids him. While touring the Laurelorn to drum up support for attacks on the Elves, Kochler is escorted by a band of sycophantic woodsmen with axes to grind. The most loyal of these call themselves the Jolly Axemen. 

Nurgle’s favour was bestowed upon the merchant four years prior to the current outbreak. The Daemon Mulch-Rot observed Kochler walking in the woods and made him the first human to receive the gift of Eyeslime Fever. Herr Kochler fell sick and complained to all the gods, but only Nurgle would hear him. 

On the seventh night, Kochler was offered a deal by Mulch-Rot, who came in the guise of a rotten walking tree. The delirious merchant agreed readily, though he’s since forgotten the terms of his bargain. 

The sickness left Kochler with bald patches in his curly black hair, which he covers by wearing a large, gaudy hat. His skin is pale and clammy, and he frequently rubs his hands together as if anticipating something. Herr Kochler spreads misinformation about the plague to incriminate Elves and cause a wider conflict in the Laurelorn. Suitably articulate foresters are inducted into Kochler’s cult with a short ritual — little more than a handshake — that makes recipients immune to the symptoms of Eyeslime Fever, but also begins a process of internal rot. 

## **Mulch-Rot**
## **Herald of Grubile**
The Plaguebearer that brought Eyeslime Fever is a grotesque pot-bellied cyclops covered in fungal cysts. Mulch-Rot was birthed from the mournful souls of drowning swamp trees. In the mortal realm, Mulch-Rot possesses the husks of trees, which begin to rot within days and grow thick patches of mold. Other Plaguebearers gather around scraping eagerly at MulchRot’s mould for their own infections. This mould is the Red Blight which infects certain trees in the Laurelorn. Though it will slowly rot trees infected by it, its true danger is in spreading Eyeslime Fever. 

Mulch-Rot’s daemonic underlings cannot venture far from Ammenvale without losing stability, so they dispatch cultist allies to propagate their mold spores. Grubile’s herald is more resilient, having ventured as far as Vesterrup to deliver the fever. On these excursions, Mulch-Rot spreads Grubile’s spores, causing many of the Spites in the vicinity to become maddened vectors of disease in the process. Human cultists require little direct guidance from Mulch-Rot, as the mortal Oswald Kochler is unnaturally gifted in Chaotic demagoguery. 

Profiles for Darlorhan, The Sons of Asuryan, Herr Oswald Kochler, and Mulch-Rot can be found in **Appendix II** . 

FOREST OF HATE IV 

## **Beginning the Adventure**
As mentioned, there are a number of ways to approach the adventure. Characters might hear of events in distant Norland in any number of ways, with rumours of plague, uprising, and strife with the elves circulating in almost any inn across the Empire. Alternatively, Characters might be dispatched to Nordland by as vaunted a personage as the Graff of Middenheim, should they be playing through **The Enemy Within** and have made his aquaintance. The Shallyan order also provides a likely hook for Characters who profess to hold more high-minded motivations. 

## **Shallyan Mission**
Nordland contains several hospices staffed by Shallyan nuns devoted to healing the sick. You can decide exactly where the hospice is located. The Shallyans seek brave adventurers to gather and distribute medicine to Zelebhorn, Hargendorf, and Skogholm (see **Plague Towns** on page 11). The order is overstretched and cannot afford to pay them. However, the kindly Sister Edelweiss claims the goddess of mercy will bestow great favour upon those who volunteer to help. 

Sister Edelweiss can provide Characters with basic background found under **Profiteers and Liars** (page 5) and **Searching for Medicine** (page 10). She advises them to start by gathering Moonflower from the Elven wood across the river from Forstfast. The other two medicines will be easier to obtain after diplomatic contact has been made with the Eonir. 

Sister Edelweiss is unaware of specific fake cures. Though she suspects Nurglish scheming, for reasons of political sensitivity she does not name Nurgle unless the Characters bring up their own previous experiences of the Ruinous Powers. Nordland’s hospices have a troubled history because their original founder, Doktor Festus, was corrupted by the Plague Lord (see the **Salzenmund** supplement for further details.) 

## **Alternative Adventure Hooks**
You might require more than one adventure hook to secure buyin from every player. Here are a few possible options in case anyone seems hesitant. 

## Nordland Politics
Relations between Nordlanders and Laurelorn Elves are often strained, but open hostilities are typically rare. The political conflict in this scenario has been orchestrated by Daemons of Nurgle. Should you wish to use this supplement without Nurglish machinations, the locations and encounters can be modified to convert the material into a bounty-hunting adventure. 

If your game is set prior to 2512 IC, Baron Werner Nikse is Grand Count of Nordland. The Enemy Within campaign results in Theoderic Gausser usurping Nikse to become Nordland’s first Elector Count in over 300 years. However, the Margravinate of Forstmark (described in the gazetteer section) remains Nikse land even after Werner’s defeat. Further details on Nordland politics can be found in **Salzenmund: City of Salt and Silver** . 

- **Personal Stakes** : One of the Characters (or a friendly NPC) has fallen ill. 

- **Bounty Hunting:** Rumours circulate of rich bounties being offered in the Laurelorn. 

- **Selling Medicine** : Characters can sell medicine in the three Plague Towns. 

## **Searching for Medicine**
Moonflower, Fire Nettles, and Bluebells are used as medicine to alleviate individual symptoms of Eyeslime Fever. Moonflower reduces the infection’s duration, Fire Nettles prevent the fever from leaving permanent scars, and Bluebells soothe the eyes improving vision. Characters that distribute all three of these medicines at all three Plague Towns earn a Fate Point. Moonflower can be picked in the Golden Wood (#5). Fire Nettles can be picked at Kor Immarmor (#8). Bluebells can be picked in the Silver Hills during springtime or purchased at Schlaghügel (#6) if they’re not in season. 

## **Fake Cures**
Nightshade and Monk Nose are fake cures being promoted by the Nordland Foresters’ Guild. Characters who sell these false cures without knowing their effectiveness, or who either know or suspect that they are not effective, risk gaining Corruption, as they are ultimately doing Nurgle’s bidding. For each settlement they sell these herbs at they should make a **Challenging (+0) Cool** Test or gain 1 point of Corruption. The GM is encouraged to call for these tests after some delay to avoid alerting the player as to their source. 

Fake cures can only be identified as such through trial and error. Nightshade can be purchased in Forstfast (#3) or picked at Ammenvale (#10). Monk Nose is found at Auld Troldved (#7) and Ammenvale (#10). These locations can be found on the region map on page 20. 

## Moonflower and Lornalim Trees
Silver barked, straight trunked, and bereft of their thick yellow leaves only in the very depths of winter, Lornalim trees are beloved by the elves of the Laurelorn. They grow to towering heights, and are often found covered in Moonflower — a moss which grows on the leaves of their lowest and most shaded branches. The trees are among the few which most Nordland foresters avoid cutting down under any circumstances, as to do so is to invoke the wrath of Wood Elves and more fearsome denizens of the Laurelorn alike. This has led to small stands of the tree suriving where the surrounding woods have been cleared away, though they only host Moonflower when found in the shade of a larger forest. 

## **Nightshade**
Nightshade (Belladonna) is widely used as a sedative ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 307). Large doses or long-term usage produce toxic sideeffects. Nightshade has no medicinal benefit for Eyeslime Fever, in fact it increases the disease’s mortality rate in Dwarfs. The Daemon Grubile wishes to infect as many Dwarfs as possible, as their species has proven quite resiliant to Nurgle’s ‘gifts.’ The Daemon’s mortal agent, Herr Kochler, has convinced many Dwarfs that Nightshade is legitimate medicine. 

## **Monk Nose**
Monk Nose (Fungi Mucosa) is the result of a recent discovery by Grubile, as the fetid fungus was found growing deep in the folds of his left thigh by a particularly intrepid Nurgling. The mushroom’s only purpose is to mutate Eyeslime Fever into ever more virulent strains, which can then be passed on to whoever consumes them. Grubile is using mortal cultists to distribute Monk Nose across the Laurelorn. Goblins of the local Yelloweye tribe use fertile dung in which the mutagen can grow, and trade the fungus to the cultists. Elven devotees of Asuryan have stolen samples of the mushroom at Darlorhan’s — really, Grubile’s — behest, as the Daemon hopes to produce a strain which more readily infects the Elves of the Laurelorn.

FOREST OF HATE IV 

## **Plague Towns**
The three towns most affected by Eyeslime Fever are not considered Adventure Locations for purposes of this scenario. Characters can distribute medicine to them using Endeavours, but they aren’t likely to stay for long. If they do seem to be lingering, a few encounters with moaning victims, their eyes covered in bandages that barely conceal the bloody pus that stains their visage, should see most parties on their way. 

## **Zelebhorn**
Zelebhorn is currently the site of a military checkpoint and isolation camp. Nordland and Middenland soldiers inspect travelers for symptoms and advise on safety protocols. Southbound travelers are redirected to the isolation camp where they must remain for three days without symptoms. The town’s sawmills are closed because of the plague. Two Jolly Axemen (see Appendix) loiter about promoting bogus cures and teaching anti-Elven slurs to idle mill workers. 

## **Skogholm**
The smaller of the two Nikse border fortresses was constructed by Dwarf masons and is maintained by their descendants. Inside the fort is a village of low houses with extensive underground quarters. Secret tunnels extend for miles beneath the forest into the Elven wood. Alrik Okrisson (see Appendix) lives in Skogholm but currently operates his bounty hunting network from Forstfast. Wood Elves who’ve been victimised by the bounty hunters are planning a retaliatory attack on Skogholm in Alrik’s absence. 

Skogholm is under quarantine because its Dwarf population is devastated by the plague. Nearly fifty Dwarf deaths have spurred the demand for plague medicine, and the Dwarfs have enough gold stashed away to pay for it. The medicine market is brokered by a superstitious apothecary named Modrek who constantly makes warding signs and mutters prayers to Valaya. 

The isolation camp has turned Zelebhorn into a market town for plague medicine. Some of the wealthy travellers confined here will even pay for unproven cures. There are more charlatans in the camp than genuine physicians. The local tailor earns a tidy profit selling blindfolds for 2/- and gloves for 4/- a pair. 

## **Hargendorf**
This walled port town is the capital of the Barony of Hargenfels. Townsfolk welcome Eonir traders and tolerate religious diversity, however the plague has forced Hargendorfers into quarantine. Outside the gate is a bustling herb market and plague camp. A pair of exhausted Shallyan nuns assist the renowned physician, Doktor Greiss. The herb market is operated by a smuggling ring connected with the Hargenfels family. 

Doktor Greiss is a busy man of science with no patience for quack medicine. He will describe Eyeslime Fever’s symptoms and treatments to anyone who brings him Moonflower. While buying Moonflower in the Forstmark last week, he was chased away by Foresters’ Guild thugs. The Shallyan mission that ventured south to find a cure has not yet returned. 

## **Adventure Encounters**
_Forest of Hate_ begins with a straightforward mission to pick Moonflower in the Elven wood. Along the way, characters learn about the politics and prejudice surrounding Red Blight and Eyeslime Fever. The scenario becomes less structured after these initial challenges. GMs should modify and expand encounters according to their players’ actions. **Adventure Locations** (page 21) provides tools for more ‘sandbox’ style gameplay, as well as a guide to the climactic conclusion of Forest of Hate at Ammenvale. You will also find information on handling the fallout of the Character’s choices. 

## **Encounter Journey to Forstfast**
Adventuring parties will probably begin the scenario outside the Laurelorn forest on the Salzen road. Zelebhorn is an ideal starting point (see ‘Plague Towns’ sidebar). The first two Characters who succeed **Gossip** tests in Zelebhorn receive the following: 

- _“There’s a rush of medicine-sellers coming to the Laurelorn. Elf hair fetches 3 crowns for a lock. It’s a profiteering racket, I tell you. Even Bluebells are selling like candy.”_ 

- _“Alrik in Forstfast has a bounty on the elf called Redfern – 30 Karls is what I heard. Lots of activity in the Forstmark lately. Why can’t folks just stay the blazes home?”_ 

All subsequent **Gossip** tests generate rumours from the Plague Gossip tables (page 19). 

## **Into the Woods**
The journey from Zelebhorn to Forstfast takes two days. The first day’s travel can be narrated abstractly. Ask players to describe precautions their characters take against the plague. Characters who **Gossip** without taking precautions must roll for Eyeslime Fever infection (see Appendix). Though half of the NPCs encountered on the road are wary, an equal number are eager for human contact. 

Parties arrive in Voervinholm (#1) at dusk after passing through several Forstmark logging villages. Nobody is willing to provide boarding unless the characters offer medicine as payment. 

The party must decide whether to camp at Voervinholm or press onward to Tyrvad (#2), in which case they must roll **Endurance** tests or gain Fatigue Conditions. 

Parties can board in a Tyrvad barn for a few pennies, however the risk of infection is high and the locals are hostile to Elves. Several wanted notices are posted on a billboard in Tyrvad ( **Handout #1** ). If the party boards in Voervinholm or Tyrvad, roll for Eyeslime Fever infection as appropriate. Should the party decide to camp outdoors, 1d10+5 Maddened Spites (page 41) buzz around the perimeter of the firelight, evading any attackers. 

## **Arrival at Forstfast**
The party reaches Forstfast on the evening of day 2, or at midday if they force-marched to Tyrvad on day 1. Alrik Okrisson can be found in the village receiving scouting reports and issuing instructions to bounty hunters. Characters who eavesdrop can hear Alrik exclaim: “ _Are none of you brave enough to cross the river and find me some fresh Elf Hair?! Back in the day we called it target practice!_ ” Alrik’s background and profile are in the Appendix. 

The Dwarf rewards parties who accept the challenge with an equipment bonus of two GC paid upfront. Parties without herbalists are given a sketch of Moonflower. If the party includes an Elf, Alrik recommends they cross at the Ruined Bridge (#4). Otherwise, he introduces them to a local named Olof who can help them cross the Demst a mile downriver. 

Characters pursuing the bounties on Redfern or Snakebite ( **Handout #1** ) are warned that the fugitives are elusive and very dangerous. Redfern normally tours the Laurelorn singing at taverns, but he is now on the run. Snakebite terrorises the Silver Hills to the north with his Yelloweye Goblin warband. 

After their briefing, Characters can equip themselves for the Golden Wood expedition. The local shopkeeper Horvid accepts Elf craftwork for barter and pays 5/- apiece for Elf arrows. He cautions the party not to damage any ‘ _nice looking’_ trees. 

## **Olof Holzfäller, Bounty Hunting Woodsman**
Olof is a smiling and garrulous Jolly Axeman (see Appendix) who recently joined the Nordland Foresters’ Guild. Alrik is aware that Olof is a guild agent, though not of his ulterior motive. Although Olof dislikes Elves in general, he is friendly to Elves in the party as it serves his purposes. His mission is to spread confusion and strife by conflating the herb ‘Elf Hair’ with actual hair from Elves. Many foresters (including Olof) wear locks of Elf hair as charms to protect them from plague. These have not been gathered from willing donors. 

If Olof is helping the party cross the river, he suggests they repay him later with ‘Elf Hair’. Otherwise, after Alrik’s briefing, Olof approaches parties that include Elves, and requests to tag along for mutual protection. The duplicitous woodsman crosses the Demst often, so he’s familiar with the area. Olof has been tasked with setting a forest fire west of the river to provoke Laurelorn’s Elves. Being spotted crossing the river with the party will allow him to obscure his own involvement and pass the blame along to them. 

## **Encounter Crossing the Demst**
The Demst river must be crossed to reach Laurelorn’s inner glades. Parties can attempt crossing at the Ruined Bridge (#4) south of Forstfast, or they can use Olof ’s raft which is hidden in bushes just north of the fort. The gorges and rapids make swimming dangerous. To complicate matters, the river is inhabited by Naiads, river spirits that are sometimes playful, but more often territorial and malicious towards those that do not show them proper respect. Those with the _Second Sight_ Talent can see eddies of blue magic beneath the surface. 

The narrowest crossing is 60 yards, which takes roughly 8 rounds to swim. After 3 rounds, Naiads begin pulling characters back to the east bank. Make **Opposed Swim** tests against the Naiad’s effective strength of 45. Success means the Characters can proceed; failure means they gain a _Fatigued_ Condition for every negative SL. Characters who accumulate _Fatigued_ Conditions exceeding their **Toughness Bonus** begin drowning ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 181). If the Character stops struggling, the Naiads simply toy with them for a while before losing interest, depositing them on the east bank of the river. 

## **Rafts and Bridges**
Olof ’s raft can carry 6 passengers (or two and a horse). He cautions that Naiads will capsize the raft unless distracted during the crossing. If the party agreed to bring Olof ‘Elf Hair,’ he creates a diversion downriver while they cross without him. Characters are free to think of their own diversions — Naiads are said to find certain land dwellers intriguing, and any Character with the _River Guide_ Talent will know that singing a song to the river is enough to assuage some spirits. Having someone jump into the river will certainly work — simply throwing rocks at a distant point will not. 

Rafting across requires a **Challenging (+/-0) Row** test, which can be assisted. If the test fails, the raft capsizes 10 x -SL yards from the opposite bank. Meanwhile, Olof secretly crosses the river in a coracle. 

Parties wishing to instead cross the Ruined Bridge (#4) must negotiate with Athanoc or sneak across without drawing his attention. Most Laurelorn Elves are familiar with Athanoc, whereas outsiders must fumble their way through this encounter. Characters who fall from the bridge are deposited on the east bank by Naiads, alive or dead. Athanoc can be bribed with reports of the illegal logging camps that don’t have baronial permits at Tyrvad (#2) or Vesterrup (#9). Once satisfied, Athanoc paints three concentric circles on the faces of non-Elves, so they won’t be shot by scout patrols, and warns them to return before nightfall. Athanoc’s full profile can be found on page 40. 

## **Athanoc, Guardian Mage of the Laurelorn**
Athanoc is one of Laurelorn’s few surviving refugees from the War of the Beard. He arrived from Kor Vanaeth (now Altdorf) and lived with other refugees in the riverside caves. In that era, the bridge was made of stone. Athanoc is now a hermit with few ties. The dour guardian wears brown furs over grey robes and carries a staff of Lornalim. He is bored of gatekeeping but doesn’t trust anyone else with the responsibility. 

The guardian mage learned soul-binding magic from Darlorhan long ago. He can sense the magical disturbance at Ammenvale. In these difficult times, Athanoc allows medicine-seekers across the bridge if they are accompanied by Eonir. Other applicants must demonstrate their allegiance by providing details of logging activity in the Nikses’ lands. Illegal logging camps will be demolished by angry Tree Kin, many of whom were Athanoc’s friends and family in their former lives. 

WARHAMMER FANTASY ROLEPL AY V 

## **Encounter Searching for Moonflower**
The party only has a few hours to find Moonflower in the Golden Wood before nightfall. The Lornalim trees nearest the road and river have already been stripped by herbalists. Using Alrik’s sketch, each Character may attempt a **Challenging (+0) Survival** test every 2 hours. Success yields one Moonflower dose, along with one more for every additional SL. Characters with the **Trade (Herbalist)** skill can make an **Average (+20** ) Test instead. Individual search tests require spreading out and thus increase the risk of becoming lost. 

While Characters are searching for Moonflower in daylight, the Golden Wood is a fetching place, quite at odds with the haunted forest of children’s tales. However, at dusk eerie shadows move under the dense canopy and the birdsong goes silent. Every two hours spent searching the players will encounter one of the below events. More information on The Golden Wood can be found on page 23. 

Eonir (Forestborn) characters are approached directly by the scouts and questioned (in Eltharin) about their non-Elf companions. A couple of the scouts show signs of recent conflict, and have had rough patches shorn from their hair. If asked, they explain that they were jumped by foresters while patrolling the Elven road near Kor Immarmor. The Queen of Laurelorn has urged restraint to quell rising tensions with Humans and Dwarfs that live in the Ward of Frost. This order sits poorly with the entire patrol, especially those who were ambushed. 

## **Groves of the Elders**
Amongst the trees are groves that appear to be dead or dying. They are in fact slumbering Tree Kin (see Appendix). Elf Characters who attempt to converse with awakened Tree Kin find them unhelpful. Their spirits are only semi-coherent, and they know nothing of the plague (and care even less). NonElves who are caught in these sacred groves by Wood Elf patrols are confronted at arrow-point and told to leave the Protectorate of Laurelorn. If a Tree Kin has been attacked, the vandals are executed in a hail of arrows. 

## **Becoming Lost**

- **Elven Patrols** : The party has a 25% chance of being spotted by Wood Elf scouts. If traveling on the old Elven road, increase the chance to 50%. 

- **Groves of the Elders:** The party has a 50% chance of stumbling into a Grove of Elders every 2 hours. If searching individually, the character with the worst SL finds the grove. 

- **Becoming Lost:** Each searching character (or group) must pass an **Average (+20) Navigation** Test or become lost. After nightfall, increase to . 

- **Difficult (-10)** 

- **Forest Fire:** This encounter happens as soon as the characters decide to stop searching and return to Forstfast. It has, of course, been set by Olof. 

## **Elven Patrols**
Scout patrols of 1d10+2 Wood Elves observe the party from hiding, only revealing themselves to punish trespassers or vandals. Characters can notice hidden patrols by making an **Opposed Perception** test against their **Stealth (Rural)** of 80 (or with the **Sixth Sense** Talent). Non-Elves with facial markings from Athanoc are spared unless they harmed a Lornalim tree or a Tree Kin. Should the party fight an Eonir scout patrol, use the Wood Elf profile on **WFRP** page 311. 

Characters that become lost must spend the next two hours attempting another **Navigation** Test to retrace their steps, this time at **Challenging (+0)** difficulty. Calling out friends’ names makes the test **Average (+20)** but automatically attracts an Elven patrol (or possibly a Tree Kin at night). If the second Navigation test also fails, the character (or group) is Hopelessly Lost. These players can be taken aside for the brief “Friendly Strangers” encounter which introduces two NPC rescuers, Redfern and Katja. 

## **Forest Fire**
Whether or not the party allowed Olof to accompany them, he sets a forest fire before they can leave the Golden Wood. If Olof crossed the Demst independently in his coracle, the wily saboteur tracked the party’s location to frame them as scapegoats. If Olof was searching with the party for Moonflower, he slipped away unseen. Either way, the characters smell smoke and witness fleeing animals before they realise that a cluster of distant trees is ablaze. 

As the party decides how to react, a nearby Tree Kin (page 40) is animated by the ancient spirit Engidu. Parties that flee the scene are presumed guilty by Engidu, who gives pursuit ( _**WFRP,**_ page 166 – starting Distance 3). Should anyone stand their ground, the Tree Kin approaches an Eonir Character and asks in spirit-Eltharin: “ _Why have you brought fire to my forest!?_ ” If the party includes no Eonir characters, Engidu addresses them in Reikspiel instead. 

If the Characters are suitably respectful and explain themselves well, Engidu is merciful, as long as they agree to bring him whoever is responsible — canny parties may already suspect Olof. Before they can leave, Engidu explains just what he wants the perpetrator for: 

_‘The web of magic has been damaged by the fire, scarred and burned just as the trees have been. Bring me the coward who set these sacred woods ablaze, and I will make a balm of his soul.’_ 

Engidu requires a soul to repair the damage that the fire caused to the weave, and he will accept — or rather, demand — a substitute for sacrifice if Olof cannot be found. He tells them to bring the sacrifice to the Underwood, a system of subterranean rivers beneath the Golden Wood, and shows them one of its many entrances. If the Characters seem hesitant, Engidu adds that he is one of the Laurelorn’s oldest spirits and knows something about the source of the plague. 

Should Olof escape after setting the fire, he returns to Forstfast. Characters who search for his raft find it hidden in the bushes along with a sack containing a tinderbox and 14 empty oil flasks. Parties that return to Forstfast in pursuit of Olof will encounter Guildmaster Kochler (see “Wandering Propagandists”, page 16). Alrik is unaware of Olof ’s arson scheme, but if told about it he doesn’t seem to disapprove — were timber not needed for axe hafts and beer barrels, the old Dwarf proclaims he would have burned the forest to the ground years ago. 

## **Engidu, Ancient of the Underwood**
The natural form of this spirit, which the Characters will witness if they return with Olof or a substitute, is of a massive stag made of blistering amber light. Those with _Second Sight_ note that it exudes _Ghur_ . Engidu claims to have come to Laurelorn long before the Eonir arrived, but admits it was they who first ‘quickened’ his mind. The sprit claims to have taught Elf mages (including Darlorhan and Athanoc) many secrets, including the secrets of binding souls into Tree Kin. He has since added his strength to the Laurelorn — though the spirits there are not so bounded to these Elves as are those of Athel Loren far to the south, they still favour the Wood Elves. 

If Engidu is brought Olof, or a substitute, the unfortunate (or deserving) individual is ripped asunder in the dark caves of the Underwood, their screams audible long after their body must surely be dead. Once the Characters emerge above ground once again, the damage caused by the fire has vanished.  The ancient magic is truly primal, and counts as a Minor Exposure to Corruption, requiring a **Challenging (+0) Cool** Test to resist. 

This complete, the ancient sprit provides a cryptic clue regarding the plague: _“An ancient mistake has at last come into season, and its fruit is bitter. He who slew the Dwarfs at Kor Immarmor has paid the price a thousand times, and still it is not enough. He is imprisoned in his own cage, and a power unknown even to me whispers in his voice. The plague flows from him, though I do not know the means.”_ 

Few emotions could be more alien to a spirit such as Engidu than guilt, but the ancient being suspects his own dealings with Darlorhan may have lead the foolish mage to trust the ‘spirit’ who eventually betrayed him. As a result, Engidu is reluctant to share much more with the Characters. If asked, the strange being can reveal that ‘plague fairies’ (or any other name the Characters may have heard for Maddened Spites) are nature spirits who have grown savage due to their exposure to sickness, but adds that trying to cure them could have unintended consequences. 

## **Encounter Friendly Strangers**
The first two Characters that become ‘Hopelessly Lost’ in the Golden Wood can be rescued by NPCs. Subsequent lost characters must spend a Fate Point to survive — the Laurelorn is a dangerous place for outsiders. The Elven minstrel Redfern (see profile in Appendix) should be introduced at some stage, even if nobody becomes lost. The Human hedgewise Katja can be introduced if the party decides to kill Redfern, turn him over to Alrik, or sacrifice him to Engidu. She might also be encountered later in Schlaghügel. 

## **The Outlaw Redfern**
At a point when the party finds itself struggling for direction, they might hear music drifting through the woods. Redfern’s repertoire includes witty satires poking fun at Alrik, and epic ballads honouring Elven heroes and nature spirits. Redfern disputes Alrik’s charges ( _“He’s just sour because my aunt slew his great-great-great-great-grandfather in the War of the Beard!”_ ). Should the party apprehend Redfern to collect the bounty from Alrik, he offers to tell them what he knows about the ‘Lord of Shadows’ (who he claims is responsible for the plague) in exchange for his freedom. 

If the party seems generally sympathetic, Redfern tells them that the Nordland Foresters’ Guild is spreading Elf-hatred amongst Humans and Dwarfs in the Forstmark. Their guildmaster, Herr Kochler, owns logging camps at a village called Vesterrup near Redfern’s home glade. Redfern can guide the party to Kor Immarmor (#8) if they’re willing to protect him from bounty hunters. Hopelessly Lost Characters can be guided to the Ruined Bridge (#4). 

## **The Herb Gatherer**
Lost Characters can be found and guided to Schlaghügel (#6) by a wise herbalist who gathers medicine in the Golden Wood. Alternatively, Katja can be encountered at her cottage in Schlaghügel if the party arrives there independently. She is friendly with Wood Elves and advises Characters not to speak ill of them. Katja won’t travel to Forstfast or cross the Demst, but she will guide characters to the riverbank so they can make their own way. 

## **Katja, Hedgewise**
The middle-aged herbalist is an Old Faith worshipper who practices natural medicine. Although Eyeslime Fever hasn’t reached Schlaghügel, Katja treats patients that seek help with Bluebell. She knows that Moonflower prevents the fever from lingering and Fire Nettle roots can mitigate permanent effects. Katja finds plague profiteering distasteful, but if asked where Moonflower can be sold, she refers characters to Doktor Greiss in Hargendorf. Katja carries a gnarled walking staff and a sickle. 

Katja is familiar with the Laurelorn nature spirits. She can educate characters about Tree Kin, explaining that some are nature spirits, others vessals for Elf souls. Last month, Katja noticed a ‘strange rotted’ Tree Kin on the other side of the river from Schlaghügel, near Lake Ammen. Since then, she has confined her herb gathering to the west bank. Katja hasn’t seen any Maddened Spites, and suggests the Characters speak to the Sisters of Shallya if they attempt to discuss the Ruinous Powers. 

## **Encounter Wandering Propagandists**
After Olof sets a fire in the Golden Wood, characters are likely to be warier of the Nordland Foresters’ Guild. Coincidentally, Guildmaster Kochler is recruiting new members in the region, so the party encounters him with his Jolly Axemen when they next return to Forstfast. Presuming the characters do not kill Herr Kochler, they might cross his path again later and be offered commerce. The wandering Nurglist agitators can be introduced at any point that feels dramatically appropriate. 

## **Liars and Profiteers**
If the party didn’t catch Olof red-handed in the Golden Wood, he can be found at the Hungry Halfling inn in Forstfast accompanied by Herr Kochler and 6-10 Jolly Axemen. Olof greets the characters with a grin and denies any charges of arson. Herr Kochler interjects on his henchman’s behalf, suggesting that it was Elves who set the fire to justify a war against Laurelorn’s human foresters. He claims this was just the latest scheme in a larger Elf conspiracy. 

Herr Kochler pretends not to hear characters that contradict him, meanwhile praising sycophants as “true Nordlanders”. Challengers who don’t win an **Opposed Charm** test find themselves outnumbered by guild sympathisers amongst the inn’s clientele (including Alrik). Should a fight break out in Forstfast, a patrol of four Watchmen tries to separate combatants by grappling them. Parties will have to find better opportunities to capture Olof or engage the Jolly Axemen in fair combat. 

The cultists laugh while they fight, and favour ganging up on enemies for advantage. 

Parties that play along with Kochler are given a pamphlet ( **Handout #2** ) and a brief ‘explanation’ of plague medicine. Kochler advocates daily Nightshade dosing, and wearing charms woven from actual Elf hair. If anyone asks why Kochler doesn’t wear a charm himself, he dismisses the ‘fey curse’ as a hoax. Kochler changes the subject if anyone points out his contradictory logic. Alrik endorses Kochler’s Nightshade claims because he’s unaware of its lethal side-effects on plague-afflicted Dwarfs, but unlike the cultists, can be convinced by evidence. 

The Goblin chief Snakebite agreed to move his tribe off the land for gold, and told Kochler that the mushrooms that grow there have medicinal properties. If the Characters question the sensibility (or legality) of acquiring land like this, Kochler offers another Gold Crown each to ensure the Goblins have departed. Savvy parties might recognise an opportunity to collect the bounty on Snakebite.  Kochler has one dose of Monk Nose left, which he’ll give away for free. Characters who vocally support Kochler’s cause are given 1d10 leaflets for distribution. 

## **Encounter Guardians of Ammenvale**
## **Tracking the Cultists**
The Nordland Foresters’ Guild is easy to investigate because its outspoken members are found in every Forstmark logging village. Asking questions attracts 2-3 Jolly Axemen, who variously blame the Elves for the plague, promote bogus treatments, or deny the existence of the outbreak entirely. Not everyone likes them, but few are willing to stand up to them — especially on the off-chance that they might be right about the elves. Jolly Axemen are usually backed by a handful of regular foresters in every village. 

Parties exploring the tainted wood at Ammenvale (#10) are intercepted by a patrol of seven Sons of Asuryan (see Appendix). These radical devotees of Asuryan have doubled their patrols since the plague outbreak, to protect master Darlorhan and contain the growing corruption of the forest. Their distinctive black-and-white garb makes them visible at a distance, a marked difference to other elf patrols. The Sons can also be found at the shrine to Asuryan in Kor Immarmor (#8) at sunrise or sunset. 

## **In the Tainted Wood**
Redfern can lead parties to Vesterrup (#9) where Kochler owns logging camps and an apiary. The Jolly Axemen in Vesterrup blame Elf cultists for the taint north of their village. Curious parties are led to the tainted wood around Ammenvale (#10). An **Average (+20) Perception** Test spots torn white robes covered with dry blood on the way to these woods. The Jolly Axemen recall that a Shallyan mission came through several weeks ago. Parties that successfully follow the Shallyans’ trail (or chase Chaos Spites at night) can find Mulch-Rot and 1-2 Maddened Tree Kin near the Sanctuary at Ammenvale (see **Defeating the Nurgle Cult** , page 31). 

## **Working for Herr Kochler**
The party’s second meeting with Guildmaster Kochler is a chance encounter on the main logging road, or on the trail to Vesterrup. Herr Kochler asks them to sign a petition. The Foresters’ Guild is lobbying the Grand Baron of Nordland for unlimited logging rights east of the Demst. Kochler’s hat is askew from exertion, and he does not remember his last encounter with the party. Eonir characters make Kochler sweat nervously. 

If the party signs his petition, Herr Kochler tells them about a plot of woodland that he recently bought west of Auld Troldved (#7). He offers the characters 1 Gold Crown each to survey the forest and capture any Snotlings before his crew arrives. 

Characters might brave the tainted wood on tips from Engidu, Redfern, Katja or the Elves at Kor Immarmor. Alternatively, they might follow the Shallyans’ trail there from Vesterrup. The party is intercepted by a Sons of Asuryan patrol near the edge of the wood. Their leader steps forward to address the interlopers: “ _You should proceed no further. You will become sick_ ”. The patrol leader informs Eonir characters (in Eltharin) that a hidden villa within the wood is protected by a shield of Asuryan, but that humans have brought corruption to the woods surrounding it. 

Trusted Characters may be allowed into the tainted wood if they offer to help. At night, volunteers are tasked with walking the perimeter to watch for Maddened Spites. Characters who pursue Spites into the taint might be led directly to MulchRot (see **Defeating the Nurgle Cult** , page 31). During the day, Characters are assigned to guard five Tree Kin that slumber a mile outside the taint. Should the characters help the Sons of Asuryan they are taken to see Ammenvale if requested. 

If attacked, the Sons scatter and regroup 5 Rounds later to pick opponents off at range with arrows. Precious Elf arrows are only used against armoured opponents. The silent warriors exchange hand signals during combat. Should the patrol leader fall, any Keeper reduced to 5 Wounds must test against **Willpower** or retreat to Kor Immarmor. Their footprints can be backtracked through the tainted wood to Ammenvale. 

WARHAMMER FANTASY ROLEPL AY V 

## **At Ammenvale**
There is always a patrol of seven Sons of Asuryan guarding Ammenvale. Parties who proved helpful are shown around and assured that Asuryan protects them from corruption. Visitors are allowed into locations B and C, but not D or E — see the map on page 29. Characters will have to devise a plan to distract (or subdue) the guards if they wish to see those areas. 

In the event of combat, the Sons fight a running battle on the bridges, protecting Darlorhan at all costs. Wounded Sons fire and retreat, locking doors behind them to delay attackers. Characters with looted keys can try two per round, needing a 10+ on 1d10 (minus # of previous attempts). The three Sons on garden patrol respond five rounds after an alarm is raised. 

## **Encounter Alrik and Redfern**
Parties who worked for Alrik might be aided by the Dwarf later. Alrik can muster a team of charcoal burners to raze the tainted wood around Ammenvale. However, if Darlorhan’s corruption wasn’t exposed by smashing the crystal sarcophagus, and a Character isn’t present to mediate, Alrik’s crew is driven off by the Sons or Tree Kin. Convincing the stubborn Dwarf of Herr Kochler’s corruption and Nightshade poisoning scheme requires a **Difficult (-10) Charm** Test, even with physical evidence. 

Redfern on the other hand is eager to discredit Herr Kochler. Should the party uncover Eyeslime Fever sources at the apiary or tainted wood, Redfern can be exonerated (to Alrik’s chagrin). The grateful Elf accompanies Characters who helped him and lends testimony to their refutation of Herr Kochler. Redfern’s charisma confers a +20 bonus on any **Gossip** Tests. Redfern might suggest a counterpropaganda strategy if the Characters do not think of one themselves. 

## **Resolving the Feud**
If Redfern’s specific whereabouts are reported, Alrik will leave Forstfast (#3) to search for the outlaw. He spends a day searching, accompanied by 4 human Foresters (see Appendix). Parties that convince Alrik to venture into the woods in pursuit of Redfern might be able to show him evidence of corruption firsthand. However, Alrik is unlikely to acknowledge that the Foresters’ Guild is a cult of the Ruinous Powers. 

Should Alrik apprehend his old rival before the outlaw is exonerated, he chooses to resolve their feud by a judicial duel, adjudicated by Baron Werner Nikse personally. A few weeks later, Characters will hear that, just as the duel was set to begin, Redfern requested to play a final song before he met his fate. The music lulled the Baron, Alrik, and everyone else in attendance to sleep, before simply walking out. Alrik is said to still be in a wordless rage at the outcome. 

## **An Unholy Triad**
Three mortal pawns serve Nurgle without fully understanding the roles they play. When the party returns to the Shallyan hospice, Sister Edelweiss listens to their account and asks leading questions. Edelweiss can provide insights based upon her previous experiences with Nurglish triads, however she would prefer that Characters deduce these connections for themselves — even for a devotee of Shallya carelessly displaying knowledge of a Dark God is foolish. During any pause in the action after Ammenvale, you might encourage players to take stock of all the factions and their possible connections to the plague. 

- **Herr Kochler:** Spreads plague and propaganda to fulfil a bargain with Mulch-Rot. Incites Dwarfs whilst secretly poisoning them. Private agreements with Snakebite and the Keepers ensure plague operations can proceed. 

- **Darlorhan:** Sustains the daemonic presence around Ammenvale. Followers sow division amongst Elves. Indirectly provides ingredients for Herr Kochler’s operations. 

- **Snakebite:** Distributes mutagenic mushrooms and escalates the timber conflict. Inadvertently distracts attention away from Ammenvale and Vesterrup. 

## **Plague Gossip**
During the course of the Adventure, Characters are bound to make inquiries among the common folk of Nordland and the Laurelorn forest. You may use the Gossip tables below to determine what they hear. 

Elves suffer **-10%** when gossiping with Humans and Dwarfs (and vice versa). Rumours can be enhanced with useful details if the result is good ( **3+ SL** ) or embellished with misinformation if the die-roll is close ( **+/-0 SL** ).
