## **Wood Elf NPC Plague Gossip Table**
**1d10 Rumour** _“The Nordland Foresters’ Guild is recruiting in the_ **1-2** _Ward of Frost. They have ideas about treating Dwarfs with Nightshade and making charms of Elf hair.” “People claim Elves are immune, but that’s untrue. I_ **3-4** _had the sickness myself last month. The symptoms were mild, and easily treated with Bluebell.” “Those spites they call ‘plague faeries’ or the like are part of the natural order. I observed a swarm collecting_ **5-6** _pollen from a tree. They are merely going about their business, even if there do seem to be more of them of late.” “Baron Nikse is privately backing Alrik’s bounty_ **7-8** _hunters. Now this plague gives the baron justification to tear up our treaties and cut down the entire Laurelorn.” “The ghosts of our ancestors are the real victims here._ **9** _Athanoc says the damage to the Weave is already beyond repair in the Ward of Frost.” “This conflict is escalating quickly. Our diplomats are_ **10** _no longer welcome in Salzenmund. Skarloc the Hunter is reportedly mustering his kithband for a war with Nordland.”_ 

## **Adventure Locations**
This adventure takes place in the eastern Laurelorn Forest, called the ‘Ward of Frost’ by Elves. The following section contains background to supplement the events already presented, and can be used along with the information found in **Archives of the Empire: Vol. 1** _._ The preceding Encounters section is used alongside the information found here. When rolling to determine whether a given NPC has Eyeslime Fever, use the ‘currently sick’ percentage under Plague Status. The first percentage includes those who were sick but have since recovered, died, or were driven out of the settlement. 

Bounty notices for the Elf fugitive Redfern and the Goblin chief Snakebite are posted at the road junction (show the players **Handout #1** ). 

The Jolly Axemen urge villagers not to let the ‘fey curse’ intimidate them, and make a show of cutting down trees in the illegal camps. Elf Characters are cajoled by locals with rheumy eyes “ _hey knife-ears, let me give you a haircut…_ ” Two Jolly Axemen eagerly join any brawl that might result from such taunting. 

## **1. Voervinholm**
**Type:** Medium Village **Plague Status:** 50% have been infected; 25% currently sick 

Villagers watch for thieves and Maddened Spites (any Spites really, or even lingering wildlife, as they cannot tell them apart) from their windows. The logging camps near this predominantly Human village are legitimised by treaties with the Eonir, but they were hastily abandoned when the plague arrived. Baronial permits remain nailed to the trees and discarded axes have been left to rust amongst empty tents. The only shop is a closed Dwarf smithy owned by Kleggi Ironhand, who is bedridden in serious condition, attended to by human neighbours who either brave the disease or have recovered from it already. His family are staying with friends in the village in the hopes of avoiding infection, as Dwarfs have proven particularly susceptible. 

Most surfaces at the smithy and logging camps are covered in Red Blight, the fungus that gave rise to the first cases of Eyeslime fever, though the Characters may not know this. Nobody opens their doors to strangers. The local Jolly Axemen recently tried to recruit Kleggi’s eldest son, Foggi, to the Nordland Foresters’ Guild. However, the young smith declined because he was uncomfortable with the agitators’ divisive rhetoric. 

## **2. Tyrvad**
**Type:** Small Village **Plague Status:** 75% have been infected; 50% currently sick 

Tyrvad is located at a busy road junction connecting the two Nikse fortresses. Half of the villagers hide from the disease, while the rest carry on as normal. If questioned, they claim to be doing so to ‘ _show them Elves we won’t be intimidated._ ’ Three new logging camps operate nearby despite nightly ‘plague fey’ sightings. Tyrvad’s logging camps are considered illegal by the Eonir and their trees aren’t marked with baronial permits. 

## **3. Forstfast**
**Type:** Large Fort **Plague Status:** 5% have been infected; 2% currently sick 

This ancient border fortress is located on the east bank of the river Demst. Forstfast is strategically positioned downriver from the bridge where an old Elf road crosses from the forbidden Laurelorn heartland. Flags flying from the fortress’ square stone towers are easy to spot above the tree canopy. On the riverbank below the fortress is a small village enclosed by a sturdy wooden palisade reinforced with a small stone wall. 

Forstfast was built by Dwarfs after the Treaty of the Leaf was signed in 630 IC. Its chief purpose today is to protect Nikse forestry interests from Wood Elf intervention. The large tract of Laurelorn woodland claimed by the Nikse family is called the Margravinate of Forstmark. Most of the soldiers garrisoned at Forstfast are archers and huntsmen who patrol the Forstmark in detachments of twenty. 

- **Fortress:** The vine-covered fortress is currently under plague restrictions watched over by Shallyan nuns, which means no visitors may enter. Sheriff Blüchwalder enforces these rules strictly, which primairly ban strangers from entering the village without leave from his office. Violators are caged in the woods overnight, and survivors are usually set free the following morning. If a Nikse logging camp is raided by Elves or Tree Kin, the sheriff dispatches soldiers from Forstfast to the area. Orders are to avoid casualties on either side if possible while diplomats are sent to Marrisith, Queen of the Laurelorn, in an attempt to avoid open war. 

- **Village** : Visitor’s eyes are checked for signs of pus before being allowed inside the palisade. The Hungry Halfling inn is booked to capacity, however Alrik offers his room to the characters if they agree to work for him (Alrik has friends that he can board with). Across from the inn is Horvid’s Trading Post, which specialises in outdoor survival gear. Wood Elves occasionally trade exotic wares with Horvid. 

At present, Forstfast is being used as a base by medicine sellers and bounty hunters. Visiting herbalists gather plague medicine from the Laurelorn and sell it at Zelebhorn, Skogholm and Hargendorf. The medicine market here is poor because most inhabitants have managed to stay healthy. Alrik Okrisson pays only 1 GC per dose for Moonflower (“Elf Hair”). Nightshade (a fake cure) can be purchased here for 2 GC per dose. 

Herbalists often hire bounty hunter escorts when braving the dangerous Elf wood to gather Moonflower. Bounty hunters use herb gathering expeditions as a pretense to search for Elf fugitives. Many of these bounty hunters are unemployed woodsmen. The Nordland Foresters’ Guild is actively spreading anti-Elven propaganda and plague misinformation in Forstfast. As a result, Wood Elves are currently avoiding the fort for fear of being arrested, or having locks of their hair torn out by desperate plague victims. 

Baron Werner Nikse visits Forstfast occasionally to inspect his soldiers and appraise the plague situation. Nikse is protective of his forestland and endorses logging camps which Laurelorn’s Wood Elves consider illegal. He turns a blind eye to crimes committed against Wood Elves while sympathising with Dwarfs. Alrik Okrisson is secretly in the baron’s employ. Baron Nikse supports the Nordland Foresters’ Guild, but he’s hesitant to publicly align himself with their guildmaster. 

## **4. Ruined Bridge**
**Type:** Elven Landmark 

**Plague Status:** None 

The old Elf road from Tor Lithanel crosses the river Demst at a deep gorge. Multiple swinging bridges crisscross each other in a weave of planks and vines. The crossing is particularly treacherous because sections of planking are missing. To complicate matters, the guardian mage Athanoc has used illusion spells to turn solid sections invisible, and make gaps appear as solid planks. Athanoc can be verbally summoned from his cave in the canyon wall below. 

- **Bridge:** The first character to cross without Athanoc’s permission must attempt three **Average (+20) Initiative** tests, or else fall 20 yards into the river below (suffering 1d10+12 Wounds). After identifying illusory planks, characters can walk tightrope along the vines or attempt 5 to 7-foot Leaps over the gaps ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 166). Athanoc can, of course, reveal a safe path that requires no athletics. Horses may cross, but not carts or wagons. 

- **Athanoc’s Cave** : Five cave openings enter the canyon walls 8-12 yards below. Two caves on the opposite side lead to Athanoc’s personal quarters. The comfortably furnished abode is decorated with Elf artwork. Spell grimoires (Life, Shadows) are shelved alongside jars of arcane material components. Climbing down to the caves requires the **Scale Sheer Surface** Talent. 

Athanoc responds to greetings in the Eltharin language within 1 minute. Petitioners using other languages are ignored unless they continue pestering the guardian longer than 5 minutes. Athanoc can materialise on the opposite side of the canyon using the spell Shadowstep ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 254). Sometimes Athanoc waits until a trespasser is halfway across the bridges before he appears — mostly to amuse himself. Eonir Elves are admitted into the Golden Wood almost without question. Outsiders wishing to enter the Protectorate of Laurelorn must negotiate with the Elves for safe passage (see Athanoc’s description on page 37). 

## **5. Golden Wood**
**Type:** Large Forest **Plague Status:** None 

West of the river Demst, the Laurelorn is exclusive domain of the Elves. The Treaty of the Leaf only allows humans with the Queen’s permission to settle in the Protectorate of Laurelorn. In daylight, the Golden Wood is a joyous place of sun-dappled glades and birdsong. After sunset, it becomes a haunted forest from which trespassers rarely return. 

Since the Eyeslime Fever outbreak, herbalists have increasingly searched the Golden Wood for a cure. A medicinal moss called Moonflower is used by Elves to treat the Black Plague. Other species use Moonflower (nicknamed ‘‘Elf Hair’’) as a sedative for surgery. However, physicians have always believed that Moonflower holds undiscovered curative properties. Rules for Moonflower are covered in the **WFRP** rulebook, page 306. Its effects on Eyeslime Fever are found on page 34 of this adventure. 

- **Old Elf Road:** The road from Kor Immarmor is partially overgrown, making the Laurelorn heartland inaccessible to wagon traffic. Riders on horseback can travel normally. Characters have a 50% chance of encountering a Wood Elf patrol for every 2 hours spent travelling on the old road through the Golden Wood. 

- **Lornalim Trees:** Harming a sacred lornalim tree is punishable by death. Metallic strands in the bark of the Lornalims reflect light, which gives the Golden Wood a warm ambience in daytime but an eerie glow at night. Wizards can sense _Ghyran_ and _Chamon_ emanating from the magnificent stands. Trees near the road have already been stripped of Moonflower. Herbalists must venture at least 100 yards from the road to find the medicinal moss, which grows on the leaves. 

- **Groves of the Elders:** Amongst the Lornalims are groves that appear to be dead or dying. They are in fact slumbering Tree Kin (see Appendix). These areas are known as Groves of the Elders. Characters have a 50% chance of wandering into such a grove for every two hours spent searching the Golden Wood. At the centre of each is an Elven waystone inscribed with runes of _Ghyran_ and _Shyish_ . These ‘forest graveyards’ are hallowed ground to the Eonir. 

- **Subterranean Rivers:** Along the west bank of the Demst are cave entrances to a vast network of rivers flowing beneath the Golden Wood. A kithband of Elves belonging to the Younger ( _Harioth_ ) kindred takes refuge in the damp caverns. Eonir call these rivers the ‘Underwood’ and pay tribute to an elder spirit called Engidu who resides deep within. 

During the day, the Laurelorn’s most cruel and capricious spirits slumber inside trees. Travellers might spot an occasional Spite (page 36) but otherwise the only daytime threats are wild animals and Wood Elf patrols. At night, Spites are encountered in larger groups of 1d10+5, along with more powerful spirits, and they are often hungry. Hungry nature spirits can spontaneously manifest as Tree Kin and attack. Elves can negotiate with hungry spirits if appropriate sacrifices are offered… 

Tree Kin in the Groves of the Elders do not awaken unless they suffer at least 1 Wound, or a spell is cast upon them. Tree Kin are only awakened intentionally by Eonir mages when the forest is threatened, or when a bound Elf soul requires transfer from a deteriorating husk to a newer vessel. Elves can converse with awakened Tree Kin using a primal spirit-dialect of Eltharin. A grove near the **Ruined Bridge (#4)** contains bound Elven souls from the War of the Beard. 

Wood Elves patrol the Golden Wood vigilantly against trespassers. These guardians of the Laurelorn prefer to remain unseen to everyone except Eonir characters. Non-Elves who haven’t been marked as ‘friendly visitors’ receive a single warning, in the form of an Elven arrow lodged into a tree near their heads. Those who don’t heed this warning shot and leave the Golden Wood will be cut down with a volley of normal arrows ( **Bow Skill 49** , range 150). 

The River Demst is a natural defense against incursions from the east. Eonir that traverse the Demst in swift canoes make pacts with the Naiads for safe passage. These ‘river elves’ fight alongside the water spirits when Beastman or Goblin war parties threaten the Golden Wood. River elves also trade furs with the humans of Schlaghügel and Hargendorf. River elves are considered outsiders by other Eonir because they only settled in the Laurelorn 1,000 years ago. 

## **6. Schlaghügel**
## Laurelorn Campaign Hooks
**Forest of Hate** is a perfect springboard for fantastical adventures in the Laurelorn. Further information on the places referenced below can be found in **Archives of the Empire, Vol. 1.** 

## **The Power of Song**
The minstrel Redfern knows ancient songs that resonate with Laurelorn’s leylines. His singing can make leylines appear as rainbow pathways, visible even to those without Second Sight. Recently, Redfern has been tracking magical corruption as it sprouts up across the Laurelorn. He believes the Vale of Despair west of Tor Lithanel is spreading tendrils of dark magic through the Weave, but he doesn’t know how to stop it. Nobody has ever seen the bottom of the dreaded crevasse, meanwhile Ghost Striders who patrol the vale insist that nothing escapes their watchful gaze. 

## **Unspeakable Sacrifice**
Engidu is not the only elder spirit residing in the Underwood; even darker entities inhabit the riverside caverns. Parties might encounter a Cityborn couple from Tor Lithanel on a pilgrimage to offer themselves to the Underwood. If questioned, the Elves claim that sacrifices are necessary to preserve peace between Eonir and forest spirits and, if the spirits will it, one or both of them may escape. However, Elf characters will know that such vile practices are normally associated with the Druchii of Naggaroth. Further investigation reveals a cult of Tor Lithanel elites who’ve fallen under the enchantment of a Naggarothi sorcerer who seeks win the favour of a vile and ancient spirit. 

## **Morgrim’s Gears of War**
Lost Dwarf artifacts from the War of Vengeance have laid buried under the forest for millennia, including the remains of war machines crafted by the ancestor god Morgrim. Alrik and the other Forstmark Dwarfs have searched for generations hoping to find these ancestral relics. Morgrim’s gears are believed to be somewhere in the Misty Hills, possibly guarded by the very same Dryads and Treemen who routed the Dwarf army long ago. The thought alone is enough to set the blood of many Dwarfs boiling. 

**Type:** Medium Village **Plague Status:** None 

This idyllic village is situated on the west bank of the river Demst in violation of the Treaty of the Leaf. The von Hargenfels family colonised the site because of its proximity to an ancient stone circle. Despite the infringement on Elf territory, Schlaghügel has been allowed to remain. A few of the village’s elders were alive when the first cottage was dedicated to the goddess Rhya. 

- **Village:** Devotees of Taal, Rhya and the Old Faith try to live in harmony with the Laurelorn. Villagers place offerings at the stone circle and trade with ‘river elves’ — Eonir who bring furs down the Demst in canoes. A swinging bridge crosses over the river gorge to the east bank. Characters who inquire about plague medicine are directed to the cottage of a local hedgewise named Katja (see page 25). 

- **Stone Circle:** Atop a wooded hill 3 miles west of Schlaghügel is an ancient stone circle. Travellers are lured from the trail into thick fog by 1d10+5 Spites (see Appendix) that take the form of willo’-wisps. A **Challenging (+0) Cool** Test, opposed by the Spites **Fellowship** of 40, allows the Characters to resist the urge to follow. Any who do are sure to become lost for days — those who fail by -4 SL or more may never be seen again! 

Schlaghügel has avoided the plague despite its proximity to Ammenvale. Plague sufferers that come for treatment are given ‘blue tea’ and advised to leave an offering to Rhya at the stone circle. Characters cannot sell medicine in Schlaghügel, however Hargendorf is only a day’s journey north on the opposite side of of the river. 

## **Bluebells**
The common Bluebell (Wild Hyacinth) is a small flower native to the Silver Hills. In the springtime when Bluebells grow abundantly, herbalists only require an **Easy (+40) Outdoor Survival** test to gather doses equal to SL every 2 hours. During the rest of the year, dried Bluebell can only be purchased from herbalists who stockpiled a surplus in the spring. Characters wishing to buy Bluebells can acquire them at a cost of 10/- per dose ( there are up to 20 doses available). 

## **7. Auld Troldved**
**Type:** Small Town (Ruined) **Plague Status:** None 

The overgrown ruins of this former baronial capital are occupied by Goblins of the Yelloweye tribe, who use it as a raiding base. Crude wooden palisades and archer platforms are decorated with severed Elf heads. The woods around the ruins are infested with Snotlings. When not marauding, the Goblins live in an abandoned mine nearer the hill’s summit. The Barony of Silberhugel is now governed from Troldved, which was rebuilt at the eastern end of Lake Troldso. Their presence is tolerated only because raising an army of sufficent size to drive them out could easily spark a wider conflict between the Empire and the Wood Elves, though the situation cannot continue for long. 

- **Raiding Camp:** At any given time, the raiding camp is garrisoned by 1d10 × 20 Goblins ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 326), a quarter of which have Wolf mounts ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 317). The stench of excrement and offal is nauseating. Outsiders are met with a hail of arrows unless they have business with Boss Snakebite. 

- **Timber Plot:** West of the ruins are ten acres of Snotling-infested woodland that Snakebite sold to Herr Kochler cheaply. For every 2d10 Snotlings killed or scared off ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 326), characters can gather 1–2 Mad Cap mushrooms ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 306). Herr Kochler fancies he might find some use for the Snotlings, then harvest the timber and Mad Caps for additional profit. Wood Elves scout this hillside frequently to keep an eye on the camp. 

A **Difficult (-10) Search** test is required to find Monk Nose outside the raiding camp, where herbalists face constant harassment by Snotlings. 

## **Snakebite, Yelloweye Boss**
The Yelloweye Goblin tribe is one of several bearing that name. Their leader is a crafty negotiator called Snakebite, a creature composed mainly of vile intent and sinewy muscle. Characters seeking an audience with Snakebite can avoid being skewered by his bloodthirsty marauders if the offer is right. The Yelloweye chief is canny enough to understand that pulling some humans into his ongoing conflict with the Wood Elves from Kor Immarmor could be to his benefit. Snakebite uses the Goblin profile ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 326). 

Characters visiting on behalf of Herr Kochler are assisted with clearing the timber plot of Snotlings, as it takes very little to convince a Goblin to kick some Snotlings about. Snakebite and 20 Goblins gleefully evict their diminutive cousins from the land to expedite the sale (meanwhile keeping any Mad Caps for themselves). The entire operation only takes a couple of hours. 

Snakebite is additionally willing to trade two doses of Monk Nose for every Elf head. Characters who are spotted dealing with Snakebite by a Wood Elf patrol will have questions to answer as soon as they leave the camp. 

Goblins are immune to Eyeslime Fever. In fact, they were oblivious to the outbreak until Herr Kochler came to trade for the Monk Nose mushrooms growing in their dung piles. Although Monk Nose is a creation of Nurgle, the Goblins are not Nurgle cultists. They are simply delighted to have discovered a tasty new fungus that grows in their own dung. Characters who are seen fighting against Goblins by a Wood Elf scout patrol are welcomed to Kor Immarmor (#8) as guests. 

## **Monk Nose**
Characters wishing to obtain Monk Nose (Fungi Mucosa) can negotiate with Snakebite for access to the Goblins’ stinking midden pile. There are likely too many Goblins at the raiding camp to fight. Although Goblins did occasionally defecate on Herr Kochler’s timber plot before, Snakebite has told them to stop in order to maintain their monopoly on Monk Nose. This effort has met with only mixed success. 

## **8. Ruins of Kor Immarmor**
**Type:** Small City (Ruined) 

**Plague Status:** 50% have been infected; 25% currently sick 

A Dwarf army besieged and razed this former High Elven city 2,700 years ago. The Laurelorn forest swallowed the ruins completely before the site was eventually reclaimed by Elves. Kor Immarmor is a terraced basin built around a river. Forestborn Eonir camp in the trees overhead whilst the Cityborn inhabit a partially restored district by the river. The city’s original stonework is mostly crumbled and camouflaged by overgrowth. 

- **Perimeter Defences:** Trespassers approaching overland must navigate through briars and Fire Nettles with a **Challenging (+0) Outdoor Survival** Test. Failure means they gain one _Entangled_ and one _Poisoned_ Condition before the terraced ruins are visible. 1d10+2 Wood Elves appear in the trees overhead to interrogate trespassers from their position of advantage. 

- **Overgrown Terraces:** The terraces descending to the river are also overgrown with briars and Fire Nettles (see above). Hidden amongst the rubble are huts belonging to Elves of the Younger ( _Harioth_ ) Kindred. They have been considered squatters by other Eonir since their arrival from Kislev as refugees a mere two centuries ago. 

- **Cityborn District:** On the riverbank at the base of the terrace garden are over 20 stone buildings of High Elven architecture. More than a hundred Eonir of the Cityborn ( _Toriour_ ) Kindred live here in sheltered seclusion. The district can only be accessed by river, or by bushwhacking through the perimeter defences. Notable buildings include a shrine to Asuryan, a meeting hall, and a water-powered grain mill. Sleek Elven riverboats are moored at a dock. 

The colony’s Cityborn residents are descendants of Elves who fled its destruction during the War of the Beard. These elitists consider themselves ‘true Elves’, but since there are no princes among them, Marrisith, the Queen of Laurelorn claims rulership of Kor Immarmor. The Cityborn district is a haven for radical devotees of Asuryan who oppose Laurelorn’s system of matrilineal succession. These political dissidents favour Prince Aesryn as their rightful ruler and would support a coup attempt by the Queen’s brother. 

The Forestborn perimeter guards are nomads who sleep in hammock-tents while serving their duty to the Queen. Kor Immarmor is in a dangerous region where clashes with Yelloweye Goblins occur almost daily. Lord Lindialoc (see **Archives of the Empire I** ) resupplies his kithband warriors here, but they rarely stay for long. Lindialoc’s warriors patrol the hillside to the east, meanwhile the Sons of Asuryan patrol the Lake Ammen area. 

Characters who arrive at Kor Immarmor with Redfern can bypass its perimeter defenses, but they are made to feel unwelcome by the Cityborn Eonir. Visiting Eonir (Cityborn) characters are assumed to be agents of Queen Marrisith. Eonir Characters who’ve encountered the Sons of Asuryan may attempt a **Challenging (+0) Gossip** tests to gather information about the cult of Asuryan. Though Redfern comes here frequently, he lives a wandersome lifestyle that excludes him from politics. 

The friendliest residents are the ‘bush elves’ on the terraces. If approached, they have no qualms about telling Characters (even non-Elves) stories of the ancient villa at Ammenvale. Although none of them have been there personally, they noticed that the Sons of Asuryan doubled patrols in the area since the plague outbreak. These Elves suspect illegal logging activity at Vesterrup was responsible for unleashing the plague, because it struck there first. 

## **Fire Nettles**
Laurelorn Elves imported the Fire Nettle ( _Folia Ignatus_ ) from Albion originally. Herbalists attempting to pick Fire Nettles from the perimeter defenses at Kor Immarmor are warned off by Forestborn guards. The Elves will only accept Goblin heads in exchange for their coveted plant (1 head per dose). Alternatively, herbalists can try to poach it without being noticed. Characters that enter Kor Immarmor with Redfern can pick as much as they want from the terraces. Fresh Fire Nettle weighs 1 Enc per 3 doses and must be handled with care. 

FOREST OF HATE VI 

## **9. Vesterrup**
**Type:** Small Village 

**Plague Status:** 100% have been infected; 25% currently sick 

The independent village of Vesterrup is tucked away in the foothills between three baronies. Originally settled by outlaws, the location is ideal for evading bounty hunters and tax collectors. The only overland approach is a trail from the old Elven road. Locals count on the nearby Wood Elves to deter unwanted visitors. Oswald Kochler (page 9, 37) owns a pair of illegal logging camps here. Logs are floated downriver to Hargendorf for sale. 

Vesterrup was the first Human settlement afflicted by the plague. Many villagers have suffered permanent scarring around their eyes, hair loss and anaemia. Herr Kochler has convinced them that the plague is a test to separate the strong from the weak, and should be embraced. They are unaware that he is a cultist of Nurgle — something which Herr Kochler is only intermittently aware of himself. Locals know about the tainted wood at the northern end of Lake Ammen, but have drawn no connection to the disease. 

## **Herr Kochler’s Apiary & Brewery**
Herr Kochler owns an apiary set apart from the village. The beekeeper Otto is a hulking, bald brute who waddles around tending the hives. His wife Gertrude is mean and wiry, with exceptionally long fingers. They worship Nurgle but only know him as ‘Sweet Urfather’ and they regard the ‘bees’ as his sacred **WFRP** _**,**_ page creations. Both use the Mutant standard profile ( 333). Otto’s mutation (Corpulent) and the Brute Trait give him -2 Movement, +15 Strength and +15 Toughness. Gertrude’s mutation (Distended Digits) gives her +10 Dexterity. 

- **Hives:** 1d10+5 Maddened Spites (see Appendix) are concealed within the hives. If a hive is damaged or Otto is attacked, they swarm out to fight. 

- **Brewery:** Gertrude is usually making mead here. 4 jars of honey and 8 kegs of mead are ready for distribution. Consuming either the honey or the mead automatically infects a Character with Eyeslime Fever. 

- **House** : 2 Jolly Axemen (see Appendix) are posted here to guard the apiary. They arrive outside 3 rounds after a commotion is heard. 

## **10. Ammenvale**
**Type:** Large Elf Villa 

**Plague Status:** 100% have been infected; 0% currently sick 

Ammenvale contains the secret experiments of the Archmage Darlorhan, and is guarded by the Sons of Asuryan (see Appendix). Hidden within a gnarled, rotted forest is a stately villa in the High Elven style. Neatly groomed gardens form a perfect 200-yard circular clearing with the villa at its center. Visitors possessing ‘the sight’ can observe an invisible dome surrounding the gardens. The dome, which Eonir call the ‘Shield of Asuryan’, appears to repel the winds of magic, and is far older than the buildings it now contains. 

Characters can only find the Sanctuary with help of a guide, by tracking someone there, or by chasing maddened Spites. Trespassers are likely to be intercepted by a patrol of Sons of Asuryan while navigating the tainted wood. Although Eonir legends recall a forbidden sanctuary of Asuryan, few Elves have seen Ammenvale firsthand. 

- **Tainted Wood:** The tangled forest within 2 miles of Ammenvale is corrupted by Mulch-Rot, a Daemon of Nurgle, and his fellow Plaguebearers (see Appendix). Every surface is infected with Red Blight. Characters have a 50% chance per hour of encountering a Plaguebearer or Maddenned Tree Kin (see Appendix). Some Tree Kin have broken chains dangling from them, a relic of their terrible treatment. A small group of Maddened Tree Kin escaped and are hiding outside the tainted wood. The Sons of Asuryan are fighting to protect these surviving soul-vessels and understand what has happened to them. 

- **Shield of Asuryan:** Wizards can roll an **Average (+20) Perception** Test to see plumes of putrid magic rolling off the invisible dome. Lore of Nurgle spells that are cast outside the shield, but within 20 yards of it, gain +1 SL. However, daemons or undead attempting to pass through the shield disintegrate instantaneously. Characters with Corruption Points or Mutations feel a lingering pain while inside it. 

- **Sanctuary of Equilibrium:** Spellcasters immediately notice the winds of magic are faint inside the garden. Only Light wizards and priests of Asuryan can cast spells within the sanctuary. The ‘villa’ consists of three large, stone buildings connected by long bridges and surrounded by hedges. At the center of the sanctuary is a chamber housing Darlorhan’s inanimate body. 

## **Sanctuary of Equilibrium**
The sanctuary has been guarded as a holy site of Asuryan for over 2,000 years. Prior to that, Elven mages researched soul-binding techniques in the untainted environment and experimented with Laurelorn’s exotic flora. The site’s history dates back even further, to the Old Ones themselves. However, the Elves cannot ascertain its original purpose. Darlorhan’s careless bargain with Grubile the Inhabited has turned the ward that once protected the sanctuary into a siphon for Nurgle’s corruption. 

- **A. Gardens:** The well-maintained gardens are watched by three Sons of Asuryan on separate patrols. As soon as one spots a trespasser, they run to **B** or **C** to inform the guard there. The juniper and lilac hedges are 5’ high, and dense enough to conceal a party from view. Four swans swim on the pond (2 white, 2 black). If the swans are fed inequitably, they fight amongst themselves causing a great racket. 

- **B. Pyramid Hall:** The entrance is locked (Secure Door). Inside are 8 stone slabs with Elf skeletons lying on two of them. Searching reveals a small gem of solidified green magic inside each skull. Stairs ascend to the bridges. At the ceiling’s apex 20 yards overhead is a huge purple gemstone made of solidified _Shyish_ (TB 4, Wounds 6), which enables the Lore of Death to be cast inside the hall. Destroying the gem creates a brief surge of magic, awakening the Tree Kin at **C** . The pyramid is guarded by 1 Keeper. If the Shield of Asuryan drops, the skeletons awaken ( _**WFRP**_ , page 327) and vandalise the villa’s workshops ( **D** ) at Grubile’s command. 

- **C. Hall of the Sun:** The entrance is locked (Secure Door). Inside, the dome-shaped hall is illuminated through a glass skylight. Stairs ascend to the bridges. Clustered together under the skylight are 5 slumbering Tree Kin, guarded by 1 Keeper. Growing from the dirt floor are Nightshade plants (6 doses) and Monk Nose mushrooms (4 doses). If the Shield of Asuryan drops or the purple gem at B is destroyed, the Tree Kin awaken and defend the sanctuary from trespassers. 

- **D. Villa:** The ground-level entrance (Secure Door, locked) accesses the villa’s living quarters which span the first two storeys. Only the kitchen and three bedrooms were restored by the Sons of Asuryan. The remaining rooms are empty, dusty and occupied by rats. Shoe tracks through the dust upstairs can be followed to a secret door leading to the workshops. 

The third storey workshops have been unused for millennia. The doors from the bridges are locked (Normal Doors). Thick dust covers tables and workbenches, and spiderwebs cling to everything. Books were either destroyed by Darlorhan or relocated to Tor Lithanel, leaving the shelves empty. The antiquated Elven instruments are not functional but could be repaired. Three workshops are contained within the same colonnaded hall, each requiring separate **Search** tests: 

- **Alchemy Workshop:** Alchemical ingredients have long since evaporated or desiccated into useless powder. Searching disturbs three Giant Spiders ( _**WFRP,**_ page 315). If searching Characters fail a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Tests the Spiders cause Surprised Conditions as they attack. 

- **Botany Workshop:** All plant specimens have crumbled to dust. However, Darlorhan’s spore weapons survive in a dormant state and can be reactivated by exposure to magic. A successful **Average (+20) Perception** Test finds a hidden locked cupboard (TB 3, Wounds 8) containing glass jars lined with a fuzz-like substance, including 8 red (Red Blight), 5 yellow (Eyeslime Fever), and 2 green (Brain Rot). If the cupboard is destroyed by more than 2 Wounds over its limit, 1d10 jars are smashed, producing a noxious spore cloud. See **Spreading Diseases** on page 32 for consequences of tampering with dormant spores. 

- **Embalming Workshop:** An Elf skeleton lies on a workbench, arms folded across its chest. Inside the skull is a green gem that can be found with a **Search** Test. The gem is crystallised magic containing the mage’s soul, and can be used as a power source to cast spells from the Lore of Life. 

- **E. Crystal Chamber:** The slender central tower is covered with creeping vines. There is no ground-level entrance, however the doors from the bridges are unlocked (Normal Doors). Inside the tower is Darlorhan’s inanimate body encased in crystal. Atop his crystal sarcophagus is the Brazier of the Sun. Gossamer filaments connect the sarcophagus to other parts of the complex. The sarcophagus is half-covered in vines that have intruded through the tower windows. 

This apparatus, left behind by the fabled Old Ones, generates the Shield of Asuryan and is now powered by Darlorhan’s soul energy. The Keeper patrol leader awaits telepathic commands here, along with another Son of Asuryan who carries a trumpet to signal alarm. They can attempt **Perception** tests to hear commotion outside. Characters’ actions might have far-reaching consequences (see “Dropping the Forcefield” on page 31). 

- **Crystal Sarcophagus:** The crystal can sustain 10 Wounds before shattering. Darlorhan’s milky eyes open if the first blow is inadequate. The forcefield drops almost immediately after the crystal shatters, and the bridges begin to collapse. 

- **Brazier of the Sun:** The Sons of Asuryan stoke the brazier with gems of crystallised white magic. If removed, the forcefield drops after 1 hour but the bridges don’t collapse. 

- **Gossamer Filaments:** These silver threads are part of a soul-transfer network that’s no longer in use. Severing a thread causes purple magic to surge through the complex, awakening the Tree Kin at C. 

- **Vines of Blight:** The clinging vines enable Grubile to speak through Darlorhan’s body from the Realm of Nurgle. Burning or removing them only silences Grubile temporarily until they eventually regrow. 

## Power Stones
Elven mages can create gemstones made of pure, solidified magic. Power Stones are typically used to store magical energy, enchant objects, or bind souls and elementals. Using a Powerstone as an ingredient for a spell of the corresponding Lore confers **+3SL** to the **Casting** test. Other Power Stone rules are covered in the _Winds of Magic_ sourcebook. 

The green (Life) Power Stones at Ammenvale were created long ago, and therefore crumble to dust after a single use. The white (Light) and purple (Death) stones can be used 1d5 times because they were created more recently. Note that Power Stones of Elven creation are far more durable than those made by College Wizards. 

## **Conclusions & Complications**
The adventure’s climactic scene will probably occur at Ammenvale. Only by disabling the daemonic ward can the tainted wood be healed and Eyeslime Fever cured. However, Nurgle’s influence runs deep. Curing this plague lays fertile ground for other poxes to blossom. Human-Elf relations are strained in the disease’s aftermath. In the Realms of Chaos, the Nurglish daemon Grubile listens with glee to reports of the unfolding experiment. 

Mortal adventurers have a part to play in the experiment’s outcome. In the heroes’ hour of triumph, however, they will suddenly find themselves challenged with new complications. Seeds of corruption will have continued to sprout even after Mulch-Rot and Oswald Kochler were defeated. Though Darlorhan’s soul was far beyond salvation, he will already have served Nurgle admirably as a conduit of divisive and virulent ideas. War between Nordland and the Protectorate of Laurelorn might already be inevitable. 

A wide array of outcome scenarios is possible, most of which can occur either alone or in tandem. The adventure’s denouement might unfold over days (or even weeks) following its climax. At an appropriate dramatic pause after Ammenvale, players can use an Endeavour to distribute medicine to needy plague victims. Parties might then return to the Golden Wood for a new Campaign Hook, even as Nurgle’s lingering taint festers and foments discord around them. 

## **Thwarting the Shield**
The Shield of Asuryan can be lowered by removing the Brazier of the Sun or shattering the Crystal Sarcophagus. Winds of magic flood the Sanctuary when the forcefield drops, producing a 10 round magical surge that grants any channelling or casting test a +5 SL bonus. With the closure of the daemonic portal, Nurglish corruption ceases flowing into the Tainted Wood and daemons become Unstable. However, the rotting flora is still infected with Red Blight for weeks afterwards. 

- **Sons of Asuran:** If Darlorhan turns into a Chaos Spawn, surviving Sons admit they were deceived and side with the Characters. Their priority becomes ensuring the other experiments in the workshop remain undisturbed. 

- **Collapsing Bridges** : The Crystal Chamber’s destruction causes all bridges to collapse (inner bridges crumble in 5 Rounds; outer bridges last 10 Rounds). Characters on a collapsing bridge must leap to safety or fall 10 yards. 

- **Mulch-Rot’s Assault:** Mulch-Rot and seven Plaguebearers storm the unshielded Sanctuary to destroy the workshop. If unopposed, they reach the villa in 5 Rounds and demolish the building 1 minute later. 

- **Tree Kin Allies:** Awakened unaffected Tree Kin from location C might aid the characters. Each one attacks a Daemon, leaving the party to handle Mulch-Rot. Treekin combats can be resolved abstractly. Each Tree Kin has a 60% of winning their battle after 1d10+2 rounds, as the Daemons succumd to Daemonic Instability. 

- **Diseases Released:** If the jars from Darlorhan’s workshop are opened, or location D is destroyed by Mulch-Rot’s assault, new diseases might be released (see “Spreading Diseases” below). 

## **Leaving the Forcefield Intact**
Nurgle’s daemons will continue haunting the Tainted Wood for as long as the forcefield remains active, and Maddened Spites will continue spreading Red Blight. Nurgle’s children are many, and defeated Plaguebearers are easily replaced by others from Nurgle’s realm within a few days. The following consequences are time-sensitive, and if not averted, will occur after the party’s Endeavour to distribute medicine for the Shallyans. 

- **Plague!:** Red Blight and Eyeslime Fever will spread throughout Nordland and beyond unless the Tainted Wood is burnt and medicine is widely distributed (see below). Middenheim and Salzenmund bar their gates to all out of fear of the plague. The Elves are blamed for this assault, even as cooler heads attempt to ascertain the truth of the situation. Thousands perish before the outbreak is finally brought under control, but flareups continue for years afterwards. 

- **War!:** Political tensions will escalate to war between Nordland and the Wood Elves unless Oswald Kochler is defeated (see below). A surprise assault by Wood Elves and Tree Kin demolishes Skogholm, prompting Baron Nikse to deploy an army to Forstfast. Characters remaining in the area are caught in a deadly crossfire between combatants with shoot-to-kill orders. 

## **Defeating the Nurgle Cult**
Mulch-Rot can be found in the Tainted Wood by tracking the ill-fated Shallyans from Vesterrup, or by following Maddened Spites into the taint. Mulch-Rot’s branches are adorned with severed heads and limbs of Shallyan nuns, and he’s accompanied by several Plaguebearers. Disguised as a nature spirit, MulchRot might try to parley with the Characters and persuade them to investigate Ammenvale. Destroying Mulch-Rot is worth **80 XP.** Even if Mulch-Rot is destroyed, a team of charcoal burners will have to spend three days torching rotted trees and culling Maddened Spites and Tree Kin to prevent Red Blight from spreading. Burning down the Tainted Wood counts as a group Endeavour, and awards **1 Resilience Point** per character. 

Herr Oswald Kochler cannot be defeated merely by killing him; he must be publicly discredited. Characters may expose Kochler’s lies by making **Opposed Charm** tests in Forstfast to debate him. Supporting evidence may earn them a **+20** modifier. Additionally, a _Foment Dissent_ Endeavour ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 200) must be undertaken in settlements visited previously by the guildmaster. Should Kochler’s lies be exposed at Forstfast and other settlements, he counts as “defeated” and the antiElven sentiment abates somewhat. Defeating Herr Kochler temporarily averts outright war (see above) and is worth **80 XP.** Characters might be asked to testify before a travelling judge from Salzenmund. 

## **Defeating the Asuryan Cult**
The Sons of Asuryan can only be released from Grubile’s influence if their master Darlorhan is exposed as a Chaos Spawn. The tentacles that sprout from his convulsing body attack randomly, meanwhile Grubile’s laughing form becomes faintly visible where the sarcophagus was. Even if characters flee, the Spawn will be crushed beneath collapsing stonework after 5 Rounds. Putting Darlorhan to rest is worth **80 XP** . Parties that kill more than three Sons of Asuryan without exposing Darlorhan as a Spawn will find themselves being hunted by another patrol from Kor Immarmor. 

## **Distributing False Cures**
Nightshade and Monk Nose are fake cures being touted by the Nordland Foresters’ Guild. Characters who distribute these herbs without knowing if they are useful, and especially if they know they are not, are assisting Grubile’s plans. Individuals involved in the transaction must test for Corruption as described on page 10. The repercussions of trading in these useless remedies are as follows. 

- **Nightshade:** Characters who distributed Nightshade at Skogholm will be responsible for the deaths of innocent Dwarfs several days later. 

## **Distributing Medicine**
Every session, characters can earn **5-25 bonus XP** for gathering, selling and giving away legitimate medicine. Supplying all three plague medicines (Moonflower, Fire Nettle and Bluebell) to all three afflicted towns (Zelebhorn, Hargendorf and Skogholm) yields noticeable improvement in recovery and mortality rates. For saving these hundreds of lives, the goddess Shallya awards **1 Fate Point** per character. Logging activity resumes in the Forstmark at reduced levels, but the Red Blight is not entirely halted unless the Tainted Wood is burned (see above).

## **Spreading Diseases**
Intentionally spreading Eyeslime Fever, even to ones enemies, is an act of Nurglish malevolence. Perpetrators must roll a Corruption test for **Moderate Exposure** ( **WFRP** _**,**_ page 182). 

Releasing new diseases from Ammenvale’s workshop (intentionally or not) counts as **Minor Exposure** for the whole party if the experiments are exposed to magic — which they will be if the ward drops and the experiments are disturbed. These diseases may be anything the GM wishes. The unreleased pestilent infections supplied to Darlorhan during the War of the Beard have likely found other ways into the world since that time, and may be familiar poxes and plagues, or they may be something never before seen in the Empire. The GM is enocuraged to be creative in spreading Nurgle’s blessings throughout the region. 

## **Spreading Misinformation**
Nurglish propaganda from the Nordland Foresters’ Guild serves Grubile by destabilising Nordlander society and increasing vulnerability to disease. Characters who spread these lies publicly must immediately roll for Corruption, with severity decided by the GM. Blaming all Elves for the plague or conflating Moonflower with actual Elf hair counts as **Minor Exposure** . Distributing Herr Kochler’s leaflets or advocating fake cures and plague denialism counts as **Moderate Exposure.**
